summary: Granite wants the first property configured around student lease terms, early installment billing, centralized teams, accurate real-time availability, role-based access, custom leases, owner-ready reporting, rentable parking, a nonrefundable reconditioning fee, and automated maintenance workflows. turns.text: Okay. I do have a question about that. I don't know how you guys have it set up. Do you have anything? One of the issues we kind of ran into recently is, so somebody got evicted like in September. Okay. So we had went to do like a turn in the unit just because like charging the tenant for any of the damages, right? However it's been sitting empty and we signed like a new lease for it. And like with that process, like the agents like send an email to ops and maintenance about like going back out there because it's been sitting for like nine months, you know, is there anything like in your system? Like that we could do to like prompt like a new like check in of the unit or anything like that?

Yeah. So the eviction happens and then you go back in with your camera. So somebody, so ops will go in and go here's, all the damages and then they can compare the photos from the initial inspection. So are there any damages somebody puts in? The damages, puts everything in, then you go ahead and print out your eviction form. If you have to go to court, then that's all printed out nice and even. But at least you know what the total cost is. And then on the term board, the maintenance at the same time that damages are entered in, it creates a work order for maintenance. And so maintenance has a list of everything that they need to do. And then the unit becomes available again as soon as maintenance finishes their tasks.
Okay. And.
Then you're tracking how long it takes? Are you saying that unit stayed nine months vacant because it just got lost?
Well, no, we just did not have like anybody that was interested. Okay. And then we finally had someone and they went to move in. We never went back out to the unit to check it from sitting. Oh.

Yeah. So we have like there's a checklist right now that's happening where the property manager chooses how often they want to walk vacant units. So if a unit's in there vacant, then a checklist is created and then they go in, they're like every two weeks because technically, you… probably don't want to leave a unit without some type of eyeball inspection for longer than a couple of weeks because what if there's a leak? What if there's a rodent that's made its home in there? Or what if somebody left the window open, you know? And so you still want some eyeballs walking around that unit. Obviously, in our scenario, it goes to the turn board and entrata has its own turn board inside. And maintenance gets their own tasks. And so you're going to know that it's not ready because there was damages on that inspection that went out. And so it would never be a ready made unit that you could go ahead and lease because the turn hasn't completed and that maintenance hasn't happened yet. Good question though. I.

Have one other one. So as far as like turn inspection and getting the units ready to go, we're kind of in talks with having leasing or someone go in after everything's been completed to make sure it's up to standard. Nothing was missed. Do you guys have anything on your end to kind of like accommodate that or like prompted towards like, hey, like we need to go and make sure that the unit's ready to go for move in? And then like if there's any issues like something to fill out that it goes to like the team of like, hey, there's an issue with this apartment, like we need to send someone back. Like do you have anything like that?

Yeah. So there, so the inspection happens, the turn happens, all you would do is assign on your turn board is because it's completely flexible. So our system is very flexible. We wanna match your workflow and like what works best for you. And so how you operate student housing will be much different or could be completely different than how other student operators do theirs. I actually think it's a great idea to have leasing go in and go. No, I can't lease this or I can't tour this. We've got X y Z issues here. And so on the turn board, you could just have that last step on there and you just set that as a task. And so it could be like, hey, a leasing agent goes in there and that's the last thing on the turn board before the unit is ready to be leased. Again. Okay?
Okay, perfect.
